content:
Benji Okafor: final review thread for hot-route protection config schema + rollout guardrails. trying to get last sign-offs today so release can stage tomorrow. PRs:
- schema/validation: https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/18444
- feature flag + rollout controls: https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/18471

Main asks:
1) schema shape ok? any missing guardrails?
2) metric labels/cardinality concerns (esp per-route/per-tenant)
3) defaults + fail-open/closed semantics acceptable?

Jordan Lee: thanks. schema is basically in good shape. one thing i want to sanity check is the keying for route. we should be explicit that `route_key` is from our internal route registry id, not raw path templates (and definitely not full URL). otherwise we end up with ppl making per-customer routes and exploding the config + metrics.

Benji Okafor: yep, `route_key` is internal id. added comment in the JSONSchema but can add a doc note too.

Allison Grant: jumping in on metrics/cardinality. current metrics in PR use labels: `tenant_id`, `route_key`, `region`, `tier`, `reason`. tenant_id is the big red flag.

Allison Grant: we *cannot* ship a counter with tenant_id as a label in the data plane. it will blow up. we can do:
- per-route + tier + region in prod metrics (safe-ish)
- per-tenant breakdown via logs / tracing sampling (and only in support tooling)

Sergio Costa: +1. i skimmed the dashboards PR and i also saw a panel that tries to topN by tenant. that will be expensive if it’s backed by a high-card metric.

Benji Okafor: ack. i think that came from my initial draft when we were trying to debug SUP-24133. i can change instrumentation to drop tenant_id label.

Aisha Bello: please do. for SRE we mostly need “are we throttling more than expected” + “is enterprise lane healthy”. route_key + tier + region is enough to page.

Amara Diallo: from gateway side, we still need to *enforce* per-tenant/per-route limits, but that doesn’t mean we need per-tenant metrics. enforcement keys can be tenant scoped in redis, metrics aggregated.

Mina Haddad: fwiw routing team is aligned. our router queue metrics already avoid tenant label. we can emit a sampled log line when a tenant hits throttle (with request_id + tenant + route_key) and let support correlate.

Benji Okafor: ok, will do:
- metrics: `throttled_requests_total{route_key,tier,region,reason}` (no tenant)
- logs: structured throttle event includes `tenant_id` but sampled + rate limited

Allison Grant: that works. also please cap `reason` values. make it an enum not freeform string.

Jordan Lee: in schema we already have reason codes in the policy engine. maybe share list here so everyone is aligned?

Benji Okafor: current reason codes (enum) in PR:
- `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`
- `QUOTA_EXCEEDED`
- `LANE_CAPACITY`
- `BACKPRESSURE_PREFILL`
- `BACKPRESSURE_DECODE`
- `CONFIG_ERROR_FALLBACK`

Cole Summers: quota side note: `QUOTA_EXCEEDED` can be from delayed metering. are we ok with that being surfaced to customer as 429? (i know PRD says yes, but want to ensure we use Retry-After)

Amara Diallo: gateway returns 429 w/ Retry-After, and error payload includes `reason_code`. we should keep `QUOTA_EXCEEDED` distinct from `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`.

Rafael Mendes: rollout guardrails: can we ensure kill-switch is global and fast? during incident i don’t want to be flipping 3 flags.

Benji Okafor: yep. design is:
- global kill switch: `hot_route_protection_enabled=false` (bypasses policy eval)
- per-region enable: `hot_route_protection_regions=[...]`
- per-tier knobs inside config (but if global off, everything off)

Connor O'Brien: what’s propagation time for config changes? release side we need to know rollback characteristics.

Jordan Lee: policy engine cache TTL is 30s in gateway + router, config push is ~5-10s typical. so worst case ~40s until effective everywhere. kill-switch is in the same config stream.

Rafael Mendes: 40s is acceptable. please add to runbook + mention in alert playbook.

Benji Okafor: will add.

Sergio Costa: another cardinality gotcha: don’t label by `route_name` as human string if it can change. better to use stable id and map in dashboards.

Benji Okafor: using `route_key` numeric-ish id. dashboards join via static mapping in grafana vars.

Allison Grant: ok. also ensure `route_key` count is bounded (top routes list), not “any route in the system”. if someone accidentally turns this on for all routes, we’ll have like thousands.

Mina Haddad: config schema already requires explicit `routes` list, no wildcard. correct?

Benji Okafor: correct. schema:

```
{
  "version": 3,
  "enabled": true,
  "routes": [
    {
      "route_key": "chat.completions.v1",
      "regions": ["us-east-1", "eu-west-1"],
      "tiers": {
        "enterprise": {
          "lane_reserved_rps": 120,
          "max_queue_ms": 250,
          "burst_rps": 200
        },
        "self_serve": {
          "max_rps": 60,
          "burst_rps": 80
        }
      }
    }
  ],
  "defaults": {
    "retry_after_seconds": 2,
    "fail_open_on_config_error": true
  }
}
```

(note: `route_key` is internal, not path)

Allison Grant: 👍 on explicit routes.

Aisha Bello: can we add a validation rule that `routes[].regions` must be from our supported list? otherwise typos cause silent “not enforced”.

Jordan Lee: schema validator already checks against region enum. PR shows `regions` as enum array.

Benji Okafor: yep, it rejects unknown regions. also rejects unknown tiers.

Rafael Mendes: question on fail-open: i’m ok fail-open for config fetch errors *only if* we have an alert that config fetch is failing. otherwise we lose protection silently.

Benji Okafor: we added `policy_config_fetch_error_total` and a burn-rate alert in observability PR. can paste link when it merges.

Sergio Costa: does that metric have tenant label? (pls no)

Benji Okafor: no tenant label. only `component={gateway|router}` + `region`.

Connor O'Brien: for staged rollout, can we gate by allowlist of route_keys? like first 3 routes only.

Benji Okafor: yes, config is basically the allowlist. rollout will start w/ 2 enterprise routes in us-east-1 only.

Mina Haddad: last question: starvation protection. in enterprise lane we reserve capacity, but if enterprise idle, self-serve can borrow, right?

Jordan Lee: yes. reserved is a floor not a hard partition. strict priority w/ bounded starvation. when enterprise is hot, self-serve gets throttled first.

Allison Grant: ok from me once tenant_id label is removed + reason enum locked. :thumbsup:

Sergio Costa: same. remove high-card panels from dashboards, use logs for tenant drilldown. :thumbsup:

Rafael Mendes: SRE signoff contingent on (1) global kill switch documented (2) config fetch error alerts in place. :thumbsup:

Benji Okafor: got it. i’ll push updates tonight and tag for re-review. thanks all.
